title: Universo de Leyes
description:
Citation network of Mexican legal documents. Built the annotated dataset and extraction pipeline, fine-tuned RoBERTa and trained a spaCy NER model to identify legal entities and references.

Laws and their citations are shown as a knowledge graph. Paper presented at ICITS 2025. Current work uses text and graph embeddings to track how Mexican law changes over time.
publications: Valdés, F., Gomar, R. H., & Méndez, D. A. (2025). Comparative Analysis of Information Extraction Techniques in the Mexican Legal System. In Information Technology and Systems, ICITS 2025, Volume 3, Conference proceedings, Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems.

title: Ethics Survey Answer Clustering
description: Clustering of open-ended survey answers from over 200 ethics tutors in Mexico City, 10 questions each. Groups the answers automatically so investigators can relate tutor responses to student performance.

title: Futbol Transformer
description: Transformer model that treats football players and their actions as tokens in a sequence and predicts which player acts next. Built to study the architecture. In progress.

title: COSMIC NLP Automation
description:
NLP prototype that extracts COSMIC functional size points from software requirement documents. Built over two internships at Spingere: research, planning, prototyping and meetings with NLP specialists in Mexico.

Subject-verb-object triplets are extracted and an NER model classifies the verbs against real COSMIC data. F-score of 60% against expert analysis; the company continued development internally.

title: ANTAD Pharmacy Site Recommendation
description:
Site recommendation model for new pharmacy openings. Finalist, top 6 of 54 teams, ITAM Datathon 2024.

XGBoost model trained on 1,375 data points with 45 variables from INEGI open data: R² 0.9677, RMSE 23.2862. Of 1,156 municipalities, 441 rated high-potential. Recommended 46 municipalities across 20 states, a potential market of 1.33 billion pesos.

title: Gol Tempranero
description:
Analysis of whether early goals in football come from repeatable strategies. Finalist, top 5 of 120 teams, Hackathon Football Analytics ITAM 2024.

333 matches with early goals across the Bundesliga, Champions League and Copa América; the scoring team won or drew 69.3% of them. K-Means on StatsBomb play sequences (pass height, length and type) found distinct patterns by league and team.

title: SEMOVI Route Reconstruction Pipeline
description:
Pipeline that converts SEMOVI's scanned public-transport route records into geospatial routes.

Each scan is cleaned, the route text extracted with OCR, street names matched to OpenStreetMap and the path rebuilt on a map. Paper on the methods in preparation.

title: Auto-parts catalogue extraction and matching
description:
Prototype for matching automotive parts across supplier catalogues with different schemas and formats, with InvierteSustentable and JetzApp. Covers catalogue extraction, a shared category scheme and matching of compatible alternatives. The wider system tracks parts and repairs for over 300 vehicle models.

An Observer–Analyzer–Coder agent system wrote and revised Pandas code to clean catalogues digitized with Camelot and OCR. It formatted 4 of 10 brand catalogues without intervention. Inconsistent manufacturer layouts remained a limitation; the experiment is on hold.
presentations: Presented at the Centro ITAM para Datos + Algoritmos + Sociedad annual project presentation in 2024 and 2025.

title: Tellus: Geospatial ATM Expansion Planning
description:
Geospatial system for comparing candidate ATM locations. Full-stack ML engineer: spatial database, data pipeline, backend API, prediction models and map interface.

Over 12,000 ATMs with monthly transaction data from four banks. Municipality demand model R² 0.92; site transaction model R² 0.60. Identified 30 high-potential BanCoppel locations; rankings closely matched the bank's location experts.

title: Retail Informality Prioritization Model
description:
Policy-prioritization model for commercial informality in Mexico. Winner, INEGI Datatón 2025.

Combines Economic Census data with wages, social-security coverage, education, product category and regional indicators. Separates the barriers facing different products, places and business segments, and links each to a targeted policy response.

title: Teaching at MIT IAP and MIT Sloan
description: Instructor and lecturer for MIT IAP 6.S189 and 6.S187 and MIT Sloan 15.S65. Applied AI, machine learning and deployment.

title: El Critón Interactivo
description: Interactive version of Plato's Crito for first-semester students in Ideas e Instituciones Políticas I at ITAM. The narrative follows the source text and uses game design to aid recall. Custom dialogue system built in Angular.

title: Space Train
description: Personal website and portfolio, including a 3D experience. Built to learn web development and design.

title: CASAPP
description: Angular web app for tracking IB CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service) activities, used by high school classmates. Authentication, image uploads and activity management on Firebase. First substantial software project.

title: Datodos
description: Website for donating mobile data to students without home internet during the COVID-19 pandemic. Raised 2,000 pesos, covering three months of classes for five students.

title: AuthentiQR
description: Android app that checks a QR code's destination against security APIs and databases before opening it. First place, ITAM Hackathon 2023.

title: Latent Lull
description: Video game in development.

title: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe AI
description: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe engine and AI opponent for a fifth-semester Artificial Intelligence course. Minimax with alpha-beta pruning, with a neural network as the board evaluation function.

title: La Baldosa de Hisarlik
description: Unity piece that tells the Trojan Horse story from the Iliad through the images on a single excavated tile. Based on an earlier OpenGL animation.

title: Mara Triangle Safari Route Simulation
description: Rule-based agent simulation of 15 animal species in the Mara Triangle. Tests how safari vehicles on designated routes change animal behaviour and distribution.

title: Sense It
description:
"Bop It"-style game for Principles of Mechatronics, written in 2,500 lines of AVR assembly. Three analogue and two digital sensors, an Arduino as analogue-to-digital converter, timers and PWM for sound and light, and a 7-segment score display.

The game picks a sensor at random; the player must respond within a time limit that shrinks as play goes on. Laser-cut parts designed in SolidWorks.

title: Basic CPU from Logic Gates
description: 8-bit CPU built from logic gates in Quartus, with addition, subtraction and multiplication. Datapath, memory path, program counter and ALU. Connected to a breadboard with analogue inputs and a 4-digit 7-segment display.

title: 3D Scanning Course
description: Lead 3D scanner on the maker lab design team for two semesters. Taught 12 students to scan functional parts with the CR Lizard scanner and replicate or modify them in SolidWorks.

title: Hierarchical topic modeling and Tree Atlas
description:
Methods for organizing document collections into readable topic hierarchies. Grouping, parent–child structure and topic labels are handled as separate steps. Embedding and lexical representations, generated labels and bounded repairs are compared on banking questions, DBpedia texts and Mexican legal documents.

Tree Atlas shows each tree with its documents, nearest neighbours, source evidence and evaluation results. Ongoing. Some changes improve fine-grained grouping but damage broader structure; failures are kept alongside results.

title: MAKERS platform
description:
Shared platform for MAKERS' public website, orders and internal lab tools. Deliberately oversized: a small makerspace used to work through the architecture of a larger system.

pnpm and Turborepo monorepo with three Next.js apps (Site, Pedidos, Gestión) on a Django API and PostgreSQL. Shared UI components, generated API contracts, one identity model and lab permissions. Anyone can place an order; Maker membership adds hours, training and equipment permissions.

Order and production workflows, private uploads, and site administration with drafts, review, images and revision history. Migration tools and rehearsals; the new platform runs alongside the old systems during migration.

title: Mapa ITAM and the academic atlas
description:
ITAM's interactive campus map and an academic atlas of the university's research, built with the MAKERS team. The map covers room search and navigation; the atlas links faculty profiles, publications, research topics and coauthorship.

Source data collection, topic representations and linked views for people, departments, semantic neighbourhoods and collaborations. Every connection leads back to its source text. Text similarity is shown as affinity, not as a ranking of researchers.
contribution: Map development, data and atlas design

title: Espacios Latentes
description:
AI gathering at ITAM on 23 and 24 October 2026: talks, discussion and hands-on work. Co-organized through MAKERS.

Built the bilingual website and event tools with the team: registration, attendee questionnaires, organizer views and campus wayfinding.

title: Mexican parliamentary discourse
description:
Mentored MAKERS project analysing Mexican parliamentary debates.

The pipeline downloads session records, extracts interventions and links speakers to parties. Word2Vec, lexical and procedural indicators measure evidence-oriented and intuition-oriented language; a dashboard compares legislatures and parties. Exploratory measures; they do not judge argument quality or truth.

title: Artist references in music criticism
description:
Mentored MAKERS project on how Pitchfork reviewers use other artists as reference points. Combines album reviews, artist metadata and artist mentions.

Notebooks cover cleaning, artist-name matching and directed reference networks. Comparison, influence language and broader references are separated, and each link keeps its source sentence. A reference reflects the critic's framing, not historical influence.
